conviction_note: The FY26 numbers (underlying operating profit up high-teens, cash conversion near the top of 85-95%) and the first FY27 guide (high single-digit operating profit growth excluding GDT) both came out in the 17 Sep RNS, four weeks before this release. That leaves the dividend, Q1 FY27 current trading and GDT detail as the only new lines. Two UK peers confirm strong demand, but both had their good prints sold (Computacenter -7.8% on a raised outlook, Bytes about -4% intraday today). So the lean is a whisker positive (p_up 51) on a pre-released-period scale of 3.5%. The findings sum to +0.1, the same order as the scaled +0.07.

already_public.what: FY26 trading update: board expects high-teens growth in underlying operating profit (raised from mid-teens), GP growth moderately above that, cash conversion towards the top of the 85-95% range, net cash c.0.7x at end FY26. The first FY27 guide is high single-digit underlying operating profit growth excluding GDT. The prelims date of 14 Oct was confirmed.

GDT acquisition at $1,050m EV (£785m), funded by £100m cash, £550m debt (£450m RCF plus £100m term loan) and £354m equity placed at 1,890p (9.5% of share capital). Leverage 1.3x at close, new target range 0.5-1.0x. Close expected by end of Q1 CY2027.
Q3 FY26 update raised FY26 to mid-teens operating profit growth (from high single-digit) and cited memory-shortage pull-forward of orders

H1 FY26 raised FY26 to high single-digit (from low single-digit) and flagged a tougher H2 comparative. The capital allocation policy is progressive ordinary dividend, then strategic investment or return of excess capital. A £45m buyback was completed.

new_in_release.expect: FY26 underlying operating profit of about £211-214m (FY25 £180.1m × high-teens growth), in line with the 17 Sep pre-release. No change expected.

FY27 high single-digit operating profit growth ex-GDT, given only 4 weeks ago, likely reiterated. A raise is possible given peer strength (Bytes 'demand drivers strengthening') but unlikely so soon. The direction of any change is unknown.

The final ordinary dividend should be progressive. The FY26 special dividend (FY25: 16.1p) is likely cut or dropped because £100m of cash is going into GDT under a new 0.5-1.0x leverage target. Most of that is probably expected already; a special that is kept would be a mild positive.
Q1 FY27 (Aug-Sep) commentary: probably 'good start'. The risk is memory-shortage pull-forward unwinding against a tough comparative.
Guided towards the top of 85-95%, so low risk. H1 carried a £42.4m upfront customer payment that may reverse.
GDT detail, possibly IFRS-restated earnings. JP Morgan flagged revenue recognition and the US GAAP-to-IFRS conversion as the sticking point. Unknown which way this goes.

findings.finding: Two UK peers that reported after Softcat's last update confirm strong channel demand into Softcat's Q1 FY27. Bytes (H1 to 31 Aug 2026) grew GP 17.8% and GII 19.6% and says demand drivers are strengthening. Computacenter's UK Technology Sourcing GII rose 90.8% in H1 to June, with group outlook raised. This supports a confident Q1 FY27 statement or a firm FY27 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Softcat rose on guidance raises: H1 FY26 +9.2% (low-SD to HSD) and Q3 FY26 +12.8% (HSD to mid-teens). The 17 Sep raise to high-teens coincided with the deal and placing, and the stock fell 3.7% the next day. Peers in this sector sold their own good prints: Computacenter -7.8% on a record H1 with a raised outlook (Softcat -8.5% in sympathy on 8 Sep), and Bytes about -4% intraday on 13 Oct.
findings.original_quote: The demand drivers in our markets are strengthening, with software spend forecast to grow ahead of IT budgets as a whole and AI, cyber security and infrastructure the areas attracting most incremental investment.
findings.why_not_priced: Bytes released this morning and Softcat is up about 1% intraday (1,872p to 1,892p) while Bytes itself is down about 4%, so the market has not read it across as a Softcat upgrade. If it had, Softcat would be re-rating above the 1,890p placing price rather than sitting on it. This is a proxy, though, and Softcat already guided FY27 four weeks ago.
findings.independence: Computacenter 2026 Half Year Results, UK Technology Sourcing GII +90.8% and FY26 outlook raised: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/computacenter--ccc/2026-half-year-results/9759847

findings.finding: The FY26 special dividend (FY25: 16.1p, about 0.85% of spot, about £32m) is likely cut or dropped. Softcat is putting £100m of balance-sheet cash into GDT and moving to a 0.5-1.0x net debt target from c.0.7x net cash, and the 17 Sep documents say nothing on the special.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The special fell from 20.9p (FY24) to 16.1p (FY25) and the FY25 prelims still rose 4.6%. The special has not been the line this stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: analysts will have pulled the special after the deal, which is why this is sized small. The residual is the possibility that a lower ordinary payout or a scrapped special is read as balance-sheet strain. This rests on inference, not on a company statement.
findings.independence: FY25 prelims establish the special-dividend pattern and policy: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/softcat--sct/preliminary-results/9185819

findings.finding: FY26 outturn is pre-released: high-teens growth in underlying operating profit (about £211-214m on £180.1m), GP growth moderately above, cash conversion towards the top of 85-95%. Four successive upgrades make an outturn at the top of 'high-teens' likely, but it sits inside what the company told the market.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY25 prelims came after an August pre-release and moved +4.6%. The Oct 2023 and Oct 2024 prelims moved -11.9% and +10.9%, but those carried the first guide for the new year, which this year was already given on 17 Sep.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: the number was published on 17 Sep. Filed at 0 per the pre-release rule.

findings.finding: The stock sits on the 1,890p placing price after falling from 2,040p (7 Sep) and 1,968p (17 Sep). JPMorgan AM trimmed its holding from 5.55% to 5.22% after the placing. The prelims and call are the first full forum since the deal to address JP Morgan's flagged GDT concerns (earnings trajectory, revenue recognition, US GAAP to IFRS), so the bar for reassurance is low.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The deal and placing day was -3.7% to 1,895p on 15x volume. There is no prior placing-overhang print to compare.
findings.why_not_priced: The de-rating is priced. What is open is whether GDT disclosure reassures or confirms the IFRS concern, and the sign of that is genuinely uncertain, hence the wide range. JP Morgan's concerns were seen only as a search snippet (Proactive returns 403), so they are not load-bearing.

findings.finding: FY26 was flattered by memory-shortage pull-forward of orders, flagged by the company in H1 and again in Q3. FY27 faces that comparative, so the Q1 FY27 commentary carries a risk of soft phasing language against the HSD guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The H1 FY26 'tougher comparative' language did not stop a +9.2% day. The Q1 FY26 update (Nov 2025) moved -2.0%.
findings.original_quote: supported by customer demand for AI-enabled infrastructure and continued pull forward of some orders due to memory shortages
findings.why_not_priced: The FY27 HSD guide already embeds the comparative, and that guide is public. The residual is that the release's phasing language makes the guide look H2-weighted. This is a hypothesis, not a document.
